description: Tell Captain "every new Stripe payment is added as a row to my Google Sheet" and get an automation with the customer, amount in dollars and date.
answer: To send Stripe payments to Google Sheets, tell Captain "Set up an automation: every new Stripe payment is added as a row to my Google Sheet".
It builds an automation that writes only to your sheet, so nothing needs approval.
ask: Set up an automation: every new Stripe payment is added as a row to my Google Sheet with the customer, amount and date

stat.text: Stripe wants amounts in a currency's smallest unit: 1000 charges 10 USD and 10 charges 10 JPY, so a raw copy into a sheet shows the wrong figure.

steps.title: You say it in one sentence
steps.body: Name the columns you want. Captain asks which sheet to use and which currencies your payments come in.

steps.title: Captain shows you the plan
steps.body: It starts when a payment succeeds, looks up the customer, then adds a row. Refunds can be a second automation.

steps.title: You connect Stripe and Google Sheets
steps.body: Connect both once and pick the spreadsheet and tab. Put your column headings in row one so each value lands in its column.

steps.title: A payment lands, a row appears
steps.body: Each payment adds one row: date, customer name and email, amount as dollars, the currency, and the payment ID.

steps.title: Your sheet fills itself
steps.body: The sheet stays yours. Sort it, total it, chart it, or share it with your accountant.

faqs.a: Stripe has its own refund events, New Refund Created and Charge Refunded. Build a second automation on one of them that adds a refund row or updates the payment's row. Tell Captain which you prefer.

faqs.q: Why is my amount too big in the sheet?
faqs.a: Stripe sends amounts in the currency's smallest unit, so a raw copy shows cents as dollars. Ask Captain for amounts in dollars with a currency column, since yen has no cents and needs no conversion.

faqs.q: Can it add Stripe's fees to the sheet?
faqs.a: Not today. None of the Stripe actions in the catalog look up fees, so keep fees in Stripe's own reports and use the sheet for the customer, amount and date.
A payment succeeding. Stripe also has New Charge Is Created and a completed checkout session, if you want a different starting point.

faqs.q: Does it add my past payments?
faqs.a: No. It starts with the next payment after you build it. For earlier ones, export from Stripe and paste them into the sheet.
